clues.text: I was the son of Rehoboam and became king over Judah.
I reigned for three years in Jerusalem.
There was war between me and Jeroboam.
Jehovah defeated Jeroboam and all Israel before me and Judah.
My son Asa became king in my place.
Matthew's genealogy says Rehoboam became father to me, and I became father to Asa.
Rehoboam appointed me as head and leader among my brothers, intending to make me king.
I went to war with an army of 400,000 mighty, trained warriors against Jeroboam's 800,000.
I stood on Mount Zemaraim in the mountainous region of Ephraim and addressed Jeroboam and all Israel.
I said Jehovah gave David a kingdom over Israel forever by a covenant of salt.
I said Jeroboam, Solomon's servant, rose up and rebelled against his lord.
I said anyone who came along with a young bull and seven rams could become a priest of what are not gods.
I said the true God was with us, leading us, with his priests and the signal trumpets.
I chased after Jeroboam and captured Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephrain with their dependent towns.
I grew in strength, took 14 wives, and became father to 22 sons and 16 daughters.
I was laid to rest with my forefathers and buried in the City of David.
I went on walking in all the sins that my father committed prior to me.
My heart was not complete with Jehovah my God like the heart of David my forefather.
On account of David, Jehovah my God gave me a lamp in Jerusalem by raising up my son after me.
I told Israel not to fight against Jehovah the God of their forefathers, for they would not be successful.
While I spoke, Jeroboam dispatched an ambush so Judah had to fight both in front and from behind.
My people and I inflicted a great slaughter; 500,000 trained men of Israel fell.
Judah proved superior in my day because they relied on Jehovah the God of their forefathers.
Jeroboam never regained his power during my time; then Jehovah struck him down and he died.
I said idle, worthless men gathered to Jeroboam and proved superior to Rehoboam when Rehoboam was young and fainthearted.
I said Judah had not abandoned Jehovah: Aaron's descendants were ministering, and the Levites assisted in the work.
I said they made burnt offerings smoke each morning and evening, kept the layer bread on the table of pure gold, and lit the golden lampstand each evening.
The rest of my history, my deeds and my words, is recorded in the writings of the prophet Iddo.
I was the son of Omri and reigned as king over Israel in Samaria.
I took as wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal, the king of the Sidonians.
I began to serve Baal and to bow down to him.
I built a house of Baal in Samaria and set up an altar to Baal there.
Elijah the Tishbite told me that during those years there would be no dew or rain except by his word.
When I saw Elijah, I asked him if he was the one bringing great trouble on Israel.
At Elijah's word I collected the prophets together at Mount Carmel.
I asked Naboth the Jezreelite to give me his vineyard next to my palace for a vegetable garden.
After Naboth died, I got up and went down to take possession of his vineyard.
I asked King Jehoshaphat of Judah if he would go with me to fight at Ramoth-gilead.
I told Jehoshaphat that I hated Micaiah because he never prophesied good things concerning me, only bad.
I disguised myself and went into the battle at Ramoth-gilead.
I was struck between the joints of my coat of mail and died that evening.
Dogs licked up my blood by the pool of Samaria, just as Elijah had told me.
I reigned over Israel in Samaria for 22 years.
I was worse in the eyes of Jehovah than all those who were prior to me.
As if it were a trivial thing to walk in the sins of Jeroboam, I also married Jezebel and began to serve Baal.
I also made the sacred pole.
I did more to offend Jehovah the God of Israel than all the kings of Israel prior to me.
During a severe famine in Samaria, I told Obadiah to search the springs and valleys for grass to keep the horses and mules alive.
Obadiah and I divided the land between ourselves, and I went alone by one way while he went alone by another.
I had sent to nation after nation looking for Elijah and made them swear they could not find him.
When Elijah said there was the sound of a heavy downpour, I went up to eat and drink.
As a heavy downpour fell, I kept riding and made my way to Jezreel.
I told Jezebel all that Elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
When Ben-hadad besieged Samaria, I first answered that I and all that belonged to me were his.
When Ben-hadad threatened to seize all my desirable things, I refused that further demand.
I sent Ben-hadad word that the one who puts on his armor should not boast about himself like one who takes it off.
I counted 232 attendants of the princes of the provinces and 7,000 Israelite men and inflicted a great defeat on the Syrians.
After a second victory near Aphek, I called Ben-hadad my brother, had him get up into the chariot, and let him go under agreement.
Under that agreement Ben-hadad would return cities my father had lost, and I could establish markets in Damascus.
After a prophet said my life must take the place of Ben-hadad's life, I went home to Samaria sullen and dejected.
When Naboth refused me the inheritance of his forefathers, I lay down on my bed, kept my face turned away, and refused to eat.
I told Jezebel that Naboth would not give me his vineyard for money or for another vineyard.
When Elijah found me, I said, “So you have found me, O my enemy!”
After Elijah's judgment words, I ripped my garments apart, put sackcloth on my body, fasted, and walked despondently.
Because I humbled myself, Jehovah said he would not bring the calamity on my house during my lifetime, but in the days of my son.
For three years there was no war between Syria and Israel before I sought to take back Ramoth-gilead.
I gathered about 400 prophets who told me to go up against Ramoth-gilead.
I ordered Micaiah put in prison and fed with a reduced allowance of bread and water until I returned in peace.
Jehoshaphat made a marriage alliance with me, and I sacrificed sheep and cattle in abundance for him at Samaria.
I built a house of ivory and also built cities.
After I was laid to rest with my forefathers, my son Ahaziah became king in my place.
I became king over Israel in the 38th year of King Asa of Judah.
In my days Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho at the cost of his firstborn and his youngest son.
A prophet told me Jehovah was giving the large Syrian crowd into my hand that day by the attendants of the princes of the provinces, and that I would start the battle.
After the first Syrian defeat, a prophet told me to strengthen myself because the king of Syria would come up against me at the start of the next year.
At Aphek Jehovah gave the Syrians into my hand because they had said he was a God of mountains and not a God of plains.
Scripture says there had never been anyone like me, so determined to do what was bad in Jehovah's eyes, egged on by my wife Jezebel.
I acted in the most detestable way by going after the disgusting idols, just as the Amorites had done.
I said to my servants that Ramoth-gilead belonged to us, yet we were hesitating to take it back from the king of Syria.
Jehoshaphat and I sat on our thrones in royal attire at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria while the prophets prophesied before us.
I put Micaiah under oath not to speak to me anything but the truth in the name of Jehovah.
I turned Micaiah over to Amon the chief of the city and to Joash the king's son.
After I was badly wounded, I had to be propped up in the chariot facing the Syrians until I died at sunset.
I was brought to Samaria and buried there.
My daughter became the wife of Jehoram king of Judah, and he walked in the way of the kings of Israel just as those of my house had done.
Elijah ran ahead of me all the way to Jezreel after the heavy downpour began.
Twice I went home sullen and dejected: once after releasing Ben-hadad, and once after Naboth refused me his vineyard.
Jehovah said that because I let Ben-hadad escape, my life must take the place of his life; later I died facing the Syrians at Ramoth-gilead.
I searched kingdoms for Elijah in the drought years, then accused him of bringing great trouble on Israel when he finally presented himself.
After Carmel I rode to Jezreel in the downpour, then told Jezebel everything Elijah had done.
Because I humbled myself, Jehovah delayed the calamity on my house until my son's days, yet I still fell at Ramoth-gilead after ignoring Micaiah.
Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made iron horns and said I would gore the Syrians to death.
Through a marriage alliance my house was tied to Judah, and my daughter's marriage pulled Judah's king into the way of my house.
Jehovah said he would annihilate from me every male and make my house like the houses of Jeroboam and Baasha; after my death Jehu carried that out on my house.
Generations later, people were still observing the statutes of Omri and all the practices of my house.
I was the son of Jotham and became king over Judah.
I did not do what was right in Jehovah's eyes as David my forefather had done.
I walked in the way of the kings of Israel.
I made my own son pass through the fire.
Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel came up to wage war against Jerusalem in my days.
I asked Tiglath-pileser of Assyria to save me from the king of Syria and the king of Israel.
My son Hezekiah became king in my place.
Isaiah met me with a message from Jehovah during the Syrian-Israelite threat.
Matthew's genealogy says Jotham became father to me, and I became father to Hezekiah.
I was 20 years old when I became king, and I reigned for 16 years in Jerusalem.
I made metal statues of the Baals.
I made sacrificial smoke in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom and burned up my sons in the fire.
I kept sacrificing and making sacrificial smoke on the high places, on the hills, and under every luxuriant tree.
Rezin and Pekah laid siege against me but were not able to capture the city.
My heart and my people's hearts trembled like trees of the forest shaking in the wind.
I said to the king of Assyria, “I am your servant and your son.”
I took silver and gold from Jehovah's house and the king's house and sent the king of Assyria a bribe.
After seeing the altar in Damascus, I sent Uriah the priest a plan of the altar.
When I returned from Damascus, I approached the new altar and made offerings on it.
I closed the doors of the house of Jehovah.
I made altars for myself in every corner of Jerusalem.
Isaiah's vision came in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, me, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Jehovah gave me into the hand of the king of Syria, who defeated me and carried captives to Damascus.
Pekah son of Remaliah killed 120,000 in Judah in one day in my reign, all brave men.
Zichri the Ephraimite killed my son Maaseiah, Azrikam in charge of the palace, and Elkanah who was second to the king.
The Israelites took 200,000 of my people captive—women, sons, and daughters—to Samaria.
I asked the kings of Assyria for help, but Tilgath-pilneser came against me and caused me distress rather than strengthening me.
I stripped Jehovah's house, the king's house, and the houses of the princes to make a gift to Assyria, but it was of no help.
I sacrificed to the gods of Damascus that had defeated me, saying they might help me.
I cut to pieces the utensils of the house of the true God.
In all the cities of Judah I made high places for making sacrificial smoke to other gods.
I moved the copper altar from before Jehovah and put it at the north side of my own altar.
I commanded Uriah to make the morning burnt offering and the people's offerings smoke on the great altar.
I cut the side panels of the carriages into pieces, removed the basins, and took the Sea down off the copper bulls onto a stone pavement.
I shifted the covered structure for the Sabbath and the king's outer entryway away from Jehovah's house because of the king of Assyria.
They buried me in Jerusalem but did not bring me into the burial places of the kings.
Jehovah told me through Isaiah to ask for a sign as deep as the Grave or as high as the sky.
I said, “I will not ask, nor will I put Jehovah to the test.”
Edomites invaded Judah and carried off captives in my days, and Philistines raided the Shephelah and the Negeb, capturing Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo.
Jehovah humbled Judah because of me, for I had let Judah go unrestrained, resulting in great unfaithfulness.
During my distress I acted even more unfaithfully toward Jehovah.
Isaiah and his son Shear-jashub met me at the end of the conduit of the upper pool by the highway of the laundryman's field.
Isaiah told me not to fear Rezin and the son of Remaliah, calling them two stumps of smoldering logs.
Isaiah told me Syria and Ephraim plotted to appoint the son of Tabeel as king in Judah.
Isaiah said that unless I had firm faith, I would not be firmly established.
After I refused a sign, Isaiah said Jehovah himself would give a sign: a young woman would give birth to a son named Immanuel.
In the year that I died, Isaiah made a pronouncement against Philistia.
I was the son of Jehoash of Judah and became king in Jerusalem.
I continued to do what was right in Jehovah's eyes, but not with a complete heart like David.
I struck down the Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
I challenged Jehoash king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us confront each other in battle.”
Jehoash of Israel defeated me and captured me at Beth-shemesh.
After I turned away from following Jehovah, a conspiracy formed against me in Jerusalem.
I fled to Lachish, but they put me to death there.
The people of Judah made my son Azariah king in my place when he was 16 years old.
I was 25 years old when I became king, and I reigned for 29 years in Jerusalem.
My mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
I did everything as Jehoash my father had done, but not like David my forefather.
The high places were not removed in my days.
As soon as I had the kingdom firmly in my control, I killed the servants who had killed my father the king.
I did not put the sons of the murderers to death, following Moses' Law that each should die for his own sin.
I hired from Israel 100,000 mighty warriors for 100 silver talents.
A man of the true God told me not to let the army of Israel go with me, for Jehovah was not with the Ephraimites.
I asked what about the 100 talents I had given to Israel's troops; he said Jehovah could give me much more.
I dismissed the Ephraimite troops, and they returned in the heat of anger.
I captured Sela in the war, and its name became Joktheel.
After striking down the Edomites, I brought the gods of the men of Seir and bowed down to them.
Jehoash of Israel compared me to a thorny weed in Lebanon trampled by a wild beast.
I lived 15 years after the death of Jehoash king of Israel.
I registered Judah and Benjamin from 20 years old and up and found 300,000 trained warriors able to handle lance and large shield.
In the Valley of Salt I struck down 10,000 men of Seir, and Judah captured another 10,000 alive.
My men threw the captured men of Seir from the top of a crag, and they were dashed to pieces.
The dismissed troops I had sent away raided Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon, striking down 3,000 and taking spoil.
A prophet asked why I followed gods that did not rescue their own people out of my hand.
I told Jehovah's prophet, “Did we appoint you as an adviser to the king? Stop! Why should they strike you down?”
Jehovah's prophet said God had decided to bring me to ruin because I would not listen.
After capturing me, Jehoash made a breach in Jerusalem's wall from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, 400 cubits.
After capturing me, Jehoash took gold, silver, and articles from God's house and the king's house, as well as hostages, back to Samaria.
They carried me back on horses and buried me with my forefathers in Jerusalem.
Jehoash told me my heart had become arrogant after I struck down Edom, and to stay in my own house.
I did not listen to Jehoash, for this was from the true God to give us into the enemy's hand because we had followed the gods of Edom.
Articles taken from God's house when I was defeated had been with Obed-edom.
I was the son of Abijah and became king over Judah.
I did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, like David my forefather.
I removed the foreign altars and the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the sacred poles.
Jehovah defeated the Ethiopians before me and before Judah.
I removed Maacah my grandmother from her position as queen mother.
When Baasha fortified Ramah against me, I sent silver and gold to Ben-hadad of Syria.
In my old age I suffered from a disease in my feet.
My son Jehoshaphat became king in my place.
Matthew's genealogy says Abijah became father to me, and I became father to Jehoshaphat.
I reigned in Jerusalem for 41 years.
In my days the land had rest for ten years.
I expelled the male temple prostitutes from the land and removed the disgusting idols my forefathers had made.
I told Judah to search for Jehovah the God of their forefathers and to observe the Law and the commandment.
I built fortified cities in Judah while Jehovah gave me rest.
I had 300,000 from Judah with large shields and lances, and 280,000 from Benjamin with bucklers and bows.
Zerah the Ethiopian came against me with 1,000,000 men and 300 chariots and reached Mareshah.
I drew up in battle formation in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
I called to Jehovah: it does not matter to him whether those he helps are many or have no power.
Azariah son of Oded met me and said Jehovah is with you as long as you remain with him.
I took courage and removed disgusting idols from Judah and Benjamin and from cities captured in Ephraim.
I restored Jehovah's altar that was before the porch of Jehovah.
People from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon deserted to me from Israel when they saw Jehovah was with me.
We entered into a covenant to search for Jehovah with all our heart and soul.
I cut down Maacah's obscene idol, pulverized it, and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
The high places were not removed, yet my heart was complete with Jehovah all my life.
I brought into Jehovah's house the things that my father and I had made holy—silver, gold, and utensils.
Baasha built up Ramah to prevent anyone from going out or coming in to me.
I told Ben-hadad there was a treaty between me and him and between my father and his father, and asked him to break his treaty with Baasha.
When Baasha quit Ramah, I took all Judah and carried off Ramah's stones and timbers to build up Geba and Mizpah.
Hanani the seer told me I had relied on the king of Syria and not on Jehovah, so Syria's army had escaped my hand.
Hanani reminded me that because I relied on Jehovah against the Ethiopians and Libyans, he had given them into my hand.
Hanani said I had acted foolishly and from then on there would be wars against me.
I became offended at Hanani and put him in prison because I was enraged at him.
At that same time I began to mistreat others among the people.
In the 39th year of my reign I developed an ailment in my feet until I became very sick.
Even in my sickness I turned not to Jehovah but to the healers.
I died in the 41st year of my reign.
They buried me in the grand burial place I had excavated for myself in the City of David.
We pursued the Ethiopians as far as Gerar until not one of them was alive, then plundered cities around Gerar and captured flocks and camels.
In the third month of my 15th year we gathered at Jerusalem and sacrificed 700 cattle and 7,000 sheep from the spoil.
In our covenant, whoever would not search for Jehovah the God of Israel was to be put to death, whether small or great, man or woman.
There was no war until the 35th year of my reign; in the 36th year Baasha came up against me and Judah.
Hanani told me the eyes of Jehovah are roving about through all the earth to show his strength in behalf of those whose heart is complete toward him.
They laid me on a bier filled with balsam oil and specially made ointment and made an extraordinarily great funeral burning for me.
Long afterward, Ishmael threw slain men into the great cistern I had made because of Baasha of Israel.
I was the mother of Ahaziah king of Judah.
When my son died, I rose up and destroyed the entire royal line of the house of Judah.
I ruled over the land for six years.
I was Ahab's daughter who became Jehoram's wife, and he walked in the way of the house of Ahab.
After I was put to death, Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.
I was the granddaughter of King Omri of Israel.
My son was 22 years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem.
My son walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for I became his adviser in acting wickedly.
After my husband's death, people of the house of Ahab became my son's advisers, to his destruction.
When I heard the sound of the people running, I came to the people at the house of Jehovah.
I saw Jehoash standing by the pillar according to the custom, with chiefs and trumpeters.
I ripped my garments apart and cried out: “Conspiracy! Conspiracy!”
Jehoiada commanded that I not be put to death in the house of Jehovah.
They seized me, and I was put to death at the Horse Gate of the king's house.
My son was related to the house of Ahab by marriage and did what was bad like that house.
Jehoash remained hidden at the house of Jehovah for six years while I was ruling.
Jehoshabeath, wife of Jehoiada the priest and sister of Ahaziah, kept Jehoash concealed so I did not put him to death.
In the seventh year Jehoiada showed the chiefs the son of the king and made a pact with them against my rule.
When I came to the house of Jehovah, singers with musical instruments were leading the praises.
All the people of the land rejoiced and the city was quiet after I was put to death with the sword at the king's house.
I destroyed the royal line when I saw that my son had died after going to see Jehoram son of Ahab at Jezreel.
While I ruled, the only remaining royal child was hidden with his nurse in an inner bedroom, then at Jehovah's house.
I came upon a crowning at Jehovah's house: crown and Testimony on the king's son, hands clapping, “Long live the king!”
After my death the people tore down Baal's house, smashed his images, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal.
I became king over Israel in place of Nadab.
As soon as I became king, I struck down all the house of Jeroboam.
There was constant warfare between Asa and me.
I came up against Judah and began to build up Ramah.
I did what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah and walked in the way of Jeroboam.
I was the son of Ahijah of the house of Issachar.
I conspired against Nadab and struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon when I struck him down.
I put Nadab to death in the third year of King Asa of Judah and became king in his place.
I did not let remain anyone breathing who belonged to Jeroboam; I annihilated them according to Jehovah's word through Ahijah the Shilonite.
I became king in Tirzah over all Israel and reigned for 24 years.
I built up Ramah to prevent anyone from going out or coming in to King Asa of Judah.
When I heard that Ben-hadad had struck Israel's cities, I quit building Ramah and continued dwelling in Tirzah.
Asa carried off the stones and timbers of Ramah that I had been building with and built up Geba and Mizpah.
Through Jehu, Jehovah said he would make a clean sweep of me and my house, like Jeroboam's.
Jehovah said he raised me up out of the dust and made me leader over his people Israel.
Jehovah said anyone belonging to me who dies in the city the dogs will eat, and in the field the birds of the heavens will eat.
I was laid to rest with my forefathers and buried in Tirzah, and Elah my son became king.
Jehovah's word came against me both for my badness like Jeroboam's house and because I struck Nadab down.
After my death Zimri annihilated my whole house according to Jehovah's word through Jehu the prophet.
In the 36th year of Asa's reign I came up against Judah and began to build Ramah.
I was king of Syria and laid siege to Samaria.
I demanded Ahab's silver and gold and the best of his wives and sons.
After Israel's first victory, I escaped on a horse with some of the horsemen.
After the battle at Aphek I hid in an inner room.
Ahab called me his brother, had me get up into the chariot, and let me go under agreement.
I gathered my whole army with 32 other kings, horses, and chariots against Samaria.
I said about this time tomorrow my servants would search Ahab's house and seize all his desirable things.
I swore by the gods there would not be enough dust in Samaria to give each of my people a handful.
While I and the kings were drinking in the tents, I ordered an attack on the city.
I was drinking myself drunk in the tents with the 32 kings helping me when Israel came out at noon.
When men came out from Samaria, I ordered them taken alive whether for peace or for battle.
At the start of the year I mustered the Syrians and went up to Aphek for battle against Israel.
My servants said Israel's God is a God of mountains, so we should fight on level land.
At their advice I removed the kings and replaced them with governors.
My servants wore sackcloth on their hips and ropes on their heads and said, “Your servant says, 'Please, let me live.'”
I promised to return the cities my father took from Ahab's father, and that Ahab could establish markets in Damascus as my father had in Samaria.
Israel struck down 100,000 of my foot soldiers in one day, and a wall at Aphek fell on 27,000 of those left.
Ahab first answered that he and all that belonged to him were mine, then refused my further demand.
Ahab sent me word that the one who puts on his armor should not boast like one who takes it off.
Jehovah said that because we claimed he was God of mountains not plains, he would give our large crowd into Israel's hand.
We encamped opposite Israel seven days before the battle began.
When I was sick in Damascus, I sent Hazael with a 40-camel gift to inquire of Elisha whether I would recover.
I gathered 32 kings for the Samaria siege, then later replaced kings with governors before Aphek.
Jehovah had said I should be destroyed; after Ahab released me, a prophet said Ahab's life must take the place of my life.
My father's markets in Samaria became the pattern I offered Ahab for markets in Damascus.
Afterward I gathered all my army and besieged Samaria until famine made a donkey's head cost 80 silver pieces.
Jehovah caused my camp to hear chariots and a huge army; we fled, leaving tents, horses, and donkeys.
Hazael held a wet coverlet over my face until I died, and he became king in my place.
I was a Tishbite and an inhabitant of Gilead.
I told Ahab that during those years there would be no dew or rain except by my word.
Ravens brought me bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening.
Jehovah sent me to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, where a widow would supply me with food.
I told a widow that the large jar of flour would not run out and the small jar of oil would not run dry until Jehovah made it rain.
I stretched myself out over a widow's dead son three times and asked Jehovah to let the child's life come back into him.
When Ahab called me the one bringing great trouble on Israel, I said he and his father's house had brought the trouble by abandoning Jehovah's commandments and following the Baals.
I told Ahab to summon all Israel to Mount Carmel, along with the 450 prophets of Baal and the 400 prophets of the sacred pole who ate at Jezebel's table.
I asked the people how long they would keep limping between two different opinions.
I said the God who answers by fire would show that he is the true God.
I had water poured on the burnt offering three times until the trench around the altar was filled.
At my prayer fire from Jehovah fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water from the trench.
I had the prophets of Baal seized and slaughtered them at the stream of Kishon.
Jehovah's hand came on me, and I ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.
After Jezebel threatened my life, I ran for my life and came to Beer-sheba, which belongs to Judah.
Under a broom tree I asked Jehovah to take my life away, saying I was no better than my forefathers.
In the strength of angelic food I went 40 days and 40 nights to Horeb, the mountain of the true God.
I found Elisha plowing with 12 pairs of bulls and threw my official garment on him.
In Naboth's vineyard I told Ahab that dogs would lick up his blood in the place where the dogs licked up Naboth's blood.
A fiery chariot and fiery horses separated me from Elisha, and I ascended to the heavens in a windstorm.
When Jehovah was about to take me up to the heavens in a windstorm, Elisha and I went out from Gilgal.
Jehovah told me to hide at the Valley of Cherith, east of the Jordan, and drink from the stream.
After the stream ran dry because there was no rain, Jehovah sent me on to Zarephath.
At the entrance of Zarephath I asked a widow gathering wood for a little water in a cup and a piece of bread.
I told the widow first to make me a small round loaf, then to make something for herself and her son.
I carried the widow's son up to the roof chamber where I was staying and laid him on my own bed.
After Jehovah revived the widow's son, I brought him down and said, “See, your son is alive.”
In the third year Jehovah told me to present myself to Ahab, and he would send rain on the surface of the ground.
When Obadiah recognized me, I told him to go and tell his lord that I was here.
I said I was the only prophet of Jehovah left, while the prophets of Baal were 450 men.
About noon I mocked Baal's prophets, saying maybe their god was deep in thought, had gone to relieve himself, or was asleep.
I repaired the altar of Jehovah that had been torn down and built it with 12 stones for the tribes of the sons of Jacob.
I told Ahab to go up, eat and drink, for there was the sound of a heavy downpour.
On the top of Carmel I crouched with my face between my knees and sent my attendant to look toward the sea seven times.
An angel touched me under the broom tree and set before me a round loaf on heated stones and a jug of water.
When Jehovah asked what I was doing at Horeb, I said I had been absolutely zealous for Jehovah the God of armies.
I told Jehovah that Israel had forsaken his covenant, torn down his altars, and killed his prophets with the sword, and that I alone was left.
Before me a great wind, an earthquake, and a fire passed by, but Jehovah was not in them; after the fire came a calm, low voice.
Jehovah told me he still had left 7,000 in Israel whose knees had not bent down to Baal and whose mouths had not kissed him.
Jehovah told me to anoint Hazael as king over Syria, Jehu as king over Israel, and Elisha as prophet to take my place.
Elisha left the bulls, followed me, and began to minister to me.
When Ahab said, “So you have found me, O my enemy!” I answered that I had found him because he was determined to do what was bad in Jehovah's eyes.
I announced that dogs would eat up Jezebel in the plot of land of Jezreel.
I called out to Jehovah asking if he was also bringing harm to the widow with whom I was staying by putting her son to death.
After her son revived, the widow said she now knew I truly was a man of God and that Jehovah's word in my mouth was truth.
I swore to Obadiah that as surely as Jehovah of armies whom I serve is living, that day I would present myself to Ahab.
In my Carmel prayer I asked Jehovah to answer so the people would know he was turning their hearts back to him.
The seventh time my attendant reported a small cloud like a man's hand ascending out of the sea, and I told him to have Ahab hitch up before the downpour detained him.
I left my attendant at Beer-sheba and went a day's journey into the wilderness before sitting under the broom tree.
When I heard the calm, low voice, I wrapped my face in my official garment and stood at the entrance of the cave.
When Elisha asked to kiss his father and mother before following me, I told him to go and return, for what had I done to stop him?
Jehovah sent me to meet Ahab in Naboth's vineyard after Ahab went down to take possession of it.
I asked Ahab whether he had murdered a man and also taken his property.
Jehovah asked me if I had seen how Ahab humbled himself, and said he would bring the calamity on Ahab's house in the days of his son.
Jehovah's angel sent me to meet Ahaziah's messengers who were going to inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron.
I told Ahaziah's messengers he would not leave the bed on which he was lying, for he would certainly die.
Ahaziah's messengers described me as a man with a garment of hair and a leather belt around my waist.
Sitting on the top of a mountain, I twice called fire down from the heavens that consumed a chief of 50 and his 50 men.
After a third chief begged that his life be precious in my eyes, Jehovah's angel told me to go down with him and not be afraid.
I went down and personally told Ahaziah he would die because he had inquired of Baal-zebub instead of Israel's God.
Three times I told Elisha to stay behind as Jehovah sent me on to Bethel, then Jericho, then the Jordan.
I rolled up my official garment, struck the waters of the Jordan, and we both crossed on the dry ground.
Before I was taken, I told Elisha that if he saw me when I was taken from him, he would receive a double portion of my spirit.
I sent a written message to Jehoram of Judah condemning him for walking in the way of the kings of Israel and for killing his own brothers.
I announced a drought to Ahab
Ravens fed me at Cherith, a Sidonian widow fed me at Zarephath, and an angel fed me under a broom tree on the way to Horeb.
I raised a widow's son at Zarephath, then later called fire from heaven both at Carmel and against Ahaziah's companies.
I ran ahead of Ahab to Jezreel after Carmel, then fled from Jezebel's threat all the way to Beer-sheba and beyond.
At Horeb I said I alone was left, but Jehovah answered that 7,000 in Israel had not bent the knee to Baal.
Jehovah told me to anoint Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha; the first successor I actually marked was Elisha, by throwing my official garment on him.
I confronted Ahab over drought and Baal, then later found him again in Naboth's vineyard and pronounced judgment on him and Jezebel.
After I ascended, my official garment fell from me; Elisha used it to strike the Jordan and cross back over.
In my letter to Jehoram of Judah I said Jehovah would strike him with a disease of his intestines until his intestines came out.
Malachi said Jehovah would send me before the coming of the great and awe-inspiring day of Jehovah.
Malachi said I would turn the hearts of fathers back toward sons and the hearts of sons back toward fathers.
Jesus said that in my days heaven was shut up for three years and six months, and a great famine came upon the land.
Jesus said there were many widows in Israel in my days, yet I was sent only to a widow in Zarephath of Sidon.
James said I was a man with feelings like ours, yet when I prayed earnestly for it not to rain, it did not rain for three years and six months.
James said that when I prayed again, the heaven gave rain and the land produced fruit.
I appeared with Moses during Jesus' transfiguration and conversed with him.
At the transfiguration I appeared with glory and talked about Jesus' departure, which he was about to fulfill at Jerusalem.
Paul recalled my plea that I alone was left, and Jehovah's reply that he had left 7,000 men who had not bent the knee to Baal.
I asked Elijah for a double portion of his spirit.
I watched Elijah ascend to the heavens in a windstorm as a fiery chariot and fiery horses separated us.
I picked up Elijah's official garment that had fallen off him and struck the Jordan with it so I could cross.
I healed Jericho's bad water by throwing salt into the spring.
When young boys jeered at me, calling me baldhead, I cursed them in Jehovah's name, and two she-bears tore 42 of them.
I told Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan so his flesh would be restored and he would be clean.
I restored the Shunammite woman's dead son to life.
I made a borrowed axhead float after it fell into the Jordan.
I prayed for Jehovah to open my attendant's eyes, and he saw the mountainous region full of horses and war chariots of fire around me.
After I died and was buried, a dead man came to life when he touched my bones.
I used to pour out water on the hands of Elijah.
Jehovah had Elijah anoint me as prophet to take his place.
I refused to accept a gift from Naaman after he was cleansed.
At my prayer, Jehovah struck the Syrians with blindness, and I led them into Samaria.
I was the son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah.
Elijah found me plowing with 12 pairs of bulls and threw his official garment on me.
I asked to kiss my father and mother, then sacrificed a pair of bulls, boiled the meat with the plowing gear, and followed Elijah to minister to him.
I refused to leave Elijah as we went from Gilgal to Bethel, then to Jericho, and on to the Jordan.
The sons of the prophets said that the spirit of Elijah had settled down on me.
Before I prophesied for the three kings against Moab, I asked for a harpist.
I told the kings to dig trench after trench in the valley, and Jehovah filled it with water though they saw no wind or rain.
I told the king of Israel I would not look at him or take notice of him if I did not have regard for Jehoshaphat of Judah.
I told a prophet's widow to gather empty containers from her neighbors and pour oil until they were full, then sell the oil to pay her debts.
A prominent Shunammite woman made a small room on the roof for me with a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand.
I told the Shunammite woman that at that time next year she would be embracing a son.
When the sons of the prophets cried that there was death in the pot, I threw flour into it and the stew became harmless.
With 20 loaves of barley bread from Baal-shalishah, I fed 100 men, and they had some left over.
I sent word that Naaman should come to me so he might know that there is a prophet in Israel.
I pronounced that Naaman's leprosy would stick to Gehazi and his descendants forever.
I kept warning the king of Israel about places where the Syrians were coming down.
After leading the blinded Syrians into Samaria, I told the king of Israel not to strike them down but to give them bread and water and send them home.
During Samaria's siege I prophesied that by the next day a seah of fine flour and two seahs of barley would each be worth a shekel at the gate of Samaria.
I told the Shunammite woman to live as a foreigner wherever she could because Jehovah had declared a famine for seven years.
I sent one of the sons of the prophets with a flask of oil to anoint Jehu as king over Israel at Ramoth-gilead.
When I was ill with the sickness from which I died, Jehoash the king of Israel came down weeping over me.
I had Jehoash shoot “Jehovah's arrow of victory” out a window toward the east against Syria.
I grew indignant when Jehoash struck the ground with the arrows only three times.
Jesus later said that there were many lepers in Israel in my time, yet not one of them was cleansed, only Naaman the Syrian.
When Elijah was taken, I cried out, “My father, my father! The chariot of Israel and his horsemen!”
I was embarrassed into letting 50 sons of the prophets search for Elijah, though I had told them not to go.
After the incident at Bethel, I went to Mount Carmel and then returned to Samaria.
I offered to speak to the king of Israel or the chief of the army on behalf of the Shunammite woman who had gone to trouble for me.
Jehovah hid the Shunammite woman's bitter distress from me and did not tell me.
I sent Gehazi ahead with my staff to place on the Shunammite's boy's face, but the boy did not wake up.
I closed the door of the room behind myself and the Shunammite's dead boy, prayed to Jehovah, lay on him mouth to mouth, and after he sneezed seven times he opened his eyes.
Naaman came with horses and war chariots and stood at the entrance of my house, but I sent a messenger instead of coming out to him.
I asked Gehazi whether it was a time to accept silver, garments, olive groves, vineyards, sheep, cattle, or servants.
I told Gehazi that my heart was with him when Naaman got down from his chariot to meet him.
The king of Syria sent a large army by night to surround me at Dothan.
I told my attendant not to be afraid, for there were more who were with us than those who were with them.
I told the blinded Syrians, “This is not the way, and this is not the city,” then led them to Samaria.
During Samaria's famine the king of Israel swore that my head would not remain on me that day.
I told the elders that the “son of a murderer” had sent to take off my head and to hold the door of the house shut against the messenger.
I told the king's adjutant that he would see the cheap food with his own eyes but would not eat from it.
I came to Damascus while Ben-hadad the king of Syria was sick.
I told Hazael to say Ben-hadad would certainly recover, but Jehovah had shown me that he would certainly die.
I kept staring at Hazael to the point of embarrassment, then gave way to weeping.
I wept because I knew what harm Hazael would do to the people of Israel.
I told Hazael that Jehovah had shown me he would be king over Syria.
I instructed the messenger to wrap his garments around his waist, pour the oil on Jehu's head in the innermost room, then open that door and flee without delay.
When Jehoash visited me on my deathbed, he used the same cry I had used for Elijah: “My father, my father! The chariot of Israel and his horsemen!”
I laid my hands on Jehoash's hands as he put his hand to the bow.
I told Jehoash he would strike down Syria at Aphek until he finished it off.
A Syrian servant told his king that I, the prophet in Israel, was telling the king of Israel the things said in his own bedroom.
At Horeb Jehovah told Elijah that anyone escaping from Jehu's sword, I would put to death.
Before asking for a double portion, I crossed the Jordan with Elijah on dry ground after he struck the waters with his official garment.
Elijah said my request was a difficult thing and that it would happen for me only if I saw him when he was taken.
After I crossed the Jordan alone, the sons of the prophets at Jericho came to meet me and bowed down to the ground before me.
The Shunammite boy's mother told me, as I had once told Elijah, that as surely as Jehovah was living she would not leave me.
Gehazi answered me that the Shunammite woman had no son and that her husband was old.
When the Shunammite woman came to me at Mount Carmel, she grabbed hold of my feet and Gehazi came near to push her away.
My attendant asked how he could set 20 loaves before 100 men before I insisted they would eat and have some left over.
After I restored Naaman's flesh like that of a little boy, he said he knew there was no God anywhere in all the earth but in Israel.
I went with the sons of the prophets to the Jordan when they said the place where they were staying with me was too cramped.
Just as Gehazi was relating to the king of Israel how I had restored the dead one to life, the Shunammite woman arrived appealing for her house and field.
Hazael met me with a gift of every sort of good thing of Damascus, the load of 40 camels.
Though Jehovah told Elijah to anoint Hazael and Jehu, I was the one who announced Hazael's kingship and sent a messenger to anoint Jehu.
I told Jehoash that if he had struck the ground five or six times he would have finished Syria off, but now he would strike Syria only three times.
Men burying a man threw him into my burial place when they saw Moabite marauder bands at the beginning of the year.
I stayed in Jericho while the 50 men searched three days for Elijah and found nothing.
I told the men of Jericho to bring me a small new bowl with salt in it before I went out to the source of the water.
I returned from Gilgal to find famine in the land and had stew boiled for the sons of the prophets sitting before me.
I was the attendant of Elisha the man of the true God.
I chased after Naaman to take something from him after my master refused his gift.
I lied in Elisha's name so I could take silver and garments from Naaman.
Naaman's leprosy stuck to me and my descendants forever.
I went out from before Elisha a leper, white as snow.
Elisha sent me ahead with his staff to place on a dead boy's face.
When Elisha asked what could be done for the Shunammite woman, I said she did not have a son and her husband was old.
Elisha told me to call the Shunammite woman, and I called her so she stood before him.
Elisha told me to tell the Shunammite he would speak in her behalf to the king of Israel or to the chief of the army.
When the Shunammite grabbed hold of Elisha's feet, I came near to push her away.
Elisha told me to wrap my garments around my waist, take his staff, greet no one, and place the staff on the Shunammite's boy's face.
I put the staff on the Shunammite's boy's face, but there was no sound or response, and I reported that the boy did not wake up.
After Elisha restored the Shunammite's boy, he told me to call her so she could pick up her son.
I said to myself that my master had spared this Syrian Naaman by not accepting what he brought.
I told Naaman my master wanted a talent of silver and two changes of garments for two young men of the sons of the prophets from the mountainous region of Ephraim.
Naaman gave me two talents of silver and two changes of garments.
When Elisha asked where I came from, I said that I did not go anywhere.
From Mount Carmel, Elisha saw the Shunammite coming and sent me to ask whether she, her husband, and her child were well.
At Ophel I took the silver and garments from Naaman's attendants, put them in a house, and sent the men away.
Elisha asked me whether it was a time to accept silver, garments, olive groves, vineyards, sheep, cattle, or male or female servants.
Elisha said his heart was with me when Naaman got down from his chariot to meet me.
The king of Israel asked me, the attendant of the man of the true God, to relate all the great things Elisha had done.
I told the king of Israel that this was the Shunammite woman, and this was her son, whom Elisha restored to life.
I first pointed out that the Shunammite had no son; later I carried Elisha's staff ahead of him to her dead boy, but that boy did not wake up.
I asked Naaman for one talent of silver, but he urged me and I left with two talents carried before me by his attendants.
I chased Naaman, hid his gifts at Ophel, then stood empty-handed before Elisha and denied that I had gone anywhere.
While I was telling the king of Israel about Elisha restoring a dead boy, the boy's mother arrived appealing for her house and field.
The king of Israel was speaking with me when the Shunammite returned to appeal for her property after the seven-year famine Elisha had warned her about.
I was the son of Ahaz, and I became king of Judah.
I became king at 25 years of age and reigned for 29 years in Jerusalem.
I kept doing what was right in Jehovah's eyes, just as David my forefather had done.
I removed the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the sacred pole.
I crushed the copper serpent that Moses had made, because the people had been making sacrificial smoke to it.
I trusted in Jehovah the God of Israel; among the kings of Judah there was no one like me after me or before me.
I rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to serve him.
In the first year of my reign, in the first month, I opened the doors of the house of Jehovah and repaired them.
I sent word for Israel and Judah to come to Jerusalem to observe the Passover to Jehovah.
When Sennacherib invaded Judah, I went into the house of Jehovah in sackcloth and prayed.
Jehovah's angel struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp while I was under siege, and Sennacherib withdrew.
I became sick and was at the point of death, and Jehovah added 15 years to my life.
As a sign for me, Jehovah made the shadow on the stairway of Ahaz go back ten steps.
I showed the Babylonian envoys everything in my treasure-house.
I made the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city.
My son Manasseh became king in my place.
I was laid to rest with my forefathers, and Judah and Jerusalem honored me at my death.
Matthew's genealogy says Ahaz became father to me, and I became father to Manasseh.
My mother's name was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah; Chronicles also calls her Abijah.
I became king in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, the king of Israel.
I held fast to Jehovah and did not turn away from following him.
I defeated the Philistines clear to Gaza and its territories.
I told the Levites to sanctify themselves and sanctify the house of Jehovah, and to remove what was impure from the holy place.
It was my heart's desire to make a covenant with Jehovah the God of Israel.
Under my command the priests cleansed Jehovah's house, and the Levites carried the uncleanness out to the Kidron Valley.
I had the Levites stationed at Jehovah's house with cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps, by the commandment of David, Gad, and Nathan.
My princes and I decided to observe the Passover in the second month, because it could not be kept at the regular time.
When many ate the Passover without cleansing themselves, I prayed that Jehovah would make allowance for them, and he pardoned the people.
I contributed 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep for the Passover congregation.
From the days of Solomon, nothing like our great rejoicing at that Passover had happened in Jerusalem.
I commanded Jerusalem's people to give the portion due the priests and the Levites.
When I saw the heaps of contributions, I praised Jehovah and blessed his people Israel.
In Sennacherib's 14th year against me, he captured Judah's fortified cities, and I sent word to him at Lachish that I was at fault.
I gave the Assyrian king the silver from Jehovah's house and the treasuries of the king's house.
I ordered my people not to answer the Rabshakeh.
I sent Eliakim, Shebnah, and the elders of the priests in sackcloth to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
I took Sennacherib's letters, went up to Jehovah's house, and spread them out before Jehovah.
I stopped up the springs outside Jerusalem so the Assyrian kings would not find plenty of water.
Samaria was captured in my sixth year as king.
I removed the doors of Jehovah's temple and the doorposts that I myself had overlaid, and I gave them to the king of Assyria.
With determination I rebuilt the broken-down wall, raised towers, made another wall outside, and repaired the Mound of the City of David.
I told my people: with Assyria is an arm of flesh, but with us is Jehovah our God to help us and fight our battles.
The Rabshakeh took his stand by the conduit of the upper pool, at the highway of the laundryman's field, when he came against me.
I said this day was a day of distress, of rebuke, and of disgrace, for the children were ready to be born, but there was no strength to give birth.
In my prayer I asked Jehovah to save us so that all the kingdoms of the earth might know that he alone is God.
Isaiah told me Jehovah would defend Jerusalem for his own sake and for the sake of his servant David.
When Isaiah said I would die, I turned my face to the wall, wept profusely, and begged Jehovah to remember how I had walked before him faithfully and with a complete heart.
Isaiah said a cake of pressed dried figs should be applied to my boil, and I gradually recovered.
I asked whether the shadow should move forward ten steps or back ten steps, and I chose that it go back, saying the forward move would be easy.
I have a writing from when I became sick and recovered from my sickness.
After I recovered, my heart became haughty, but then I humbled myself, and Jehovah's indignation did not come in my days.
I stopped up the upper source of the waters of Gihon and directed them straight down to the west to the City of David.
Berodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent me letters and a gift because he had heard I had been sick.
When Isaiah said Babylon would carry off what was in my house, I answered that Jehovah's word was good, if there would be peace and stability in my lifetime.
My men transcribed further proverbs of Solomon.
Isaiah's vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem came in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and me.
Hosea's word from Jehovah came in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and me, kings of Judah.
Micah of Moresheth prophesied in my days, and later elders recalled that I feared Jehovah and begged for his favor rather than put Micah to death.
After Ahaz closed Jehovah's house, I opened its doors again in my first month and restored its service so suddenly that my people and I rejoiced.
I invited Ephraim and Manasseh by letter; couriers were mocked in the north, yet some from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to my Passover.
I extended that festival seven more days after the first seven, and priests and foreign residents rejoiced with Judah and Israel.
Every work I undertook to search for my God, whether the service of his house or the Law and the commandment, I did wholeheartedly, and I was successful.
I overlaid Jehovah's temple doors, later stripped that same overlay to pay Assyria, then later still Jehovah rescued my city after I spread Sennacherib's letters before him.
Jehovah gave me a sign when I was sick; later Babylon's spokesmen came to ask about that sign, and God left me alone to put me to the test.
In my writing after recovery I said the living can praise Jehovah, and that we would play my songs on stringed instruments all our days at Jehovah's house.
Isaiah told me some of my own sons would be taken and become court officials in the palace of the king of Babylon.
They buried me in the ascent to the burial places of the sons of David.
Many later brought gifts to Jehovah at Jerusalem and choice things to me, and I was greatly respected by all the nations after Jehovah saved us from Sennacherib.
I was the son of Elah and became king over Israel in Samaria.
I ruled for nine years over Israel in Samaria.
I formed a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, struck him down, and became king in his place.
In my ninth year the king of Assyria captured Samaria and led Israel into exile.
I continued to do what was bad in Jehovah's eyes, only not to the extent of the kings of Israel prior to me.
King Shalmaneser of Assyria came up against me, and I became his servant and began to pay tribute to him.
I sent messengers to King So of Egypt and did not bring the tribute up to the king of Assyria as in former years.
The king of Assyria learned of my conspiracy, kept me confined, and bound me in prison.
I became king over Israel in Samaria in the 12th year of King Ahaz of Judah.
I struck Pekah down and began to reign in his place in the 20th year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.
While I was confined, the king of Assyria invaded the entire land and laid siege to Samaria for three years.
In my ninth year Assyria captured Samaria and made the people of Israel dwell in Halah and in Habor at the river Gozan and in the cities of the Medes.
I was Ahaziah's son whom Jehosheba stole away from among the king's sons so Athaliah would not put me to death.
I remained hidden at the house of Jehovah for six years while Athaliah ruled over the land.
I was seven years old when I became king in Jerusalem.
Jehoiada put the crown and the Testimony on me, and they made me king and anointed me.
I continued doing what was right in Jehovah's eyes all the days Jehoiada the priest instructed me.
It was my heart's desire to renovate the house of Jehovah.
After Jehoiada's death I abandoned the house of Jehovah and began serving the sacred poles and the idols.
At my order they stoned Zechariah the son of Jehoiada in the courtyard of Jehovah's house.
My servants struck me down, and Amaziah my son became king in my place.
I reigned for 40 years in Jerusalem.
My mother's name was Zibiah from Beer-sheba.
I became king in the seventh year of Jehu.
In my days the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed on them.
Jehoiada chose two wives for me, and I became father to sons and daughters.
Jehoshabeath, wife of Jehoiada the priest and sister of Ahaziah, kept me concealed from Athaliah.
After Athaliah was put to death, they escorted me to the king's house and I sat on the throne of the kings.
Jehoiada made a covenant between Jehovah and me and the people, that we would continue as Jehovah's people.
By the 23rd year of my reign, the priests had not yet repaired the damage to Jehovah's house.
I called Jehoiada and the other priests and asked why they were not repairing the damage to Jehovah's house.
At my order a chest was made and placed outside at the gate of Jehovah's house for the sacred tax.
When Hazael decided to attack Jerusalem, I sent him the holy offerings and the gold from Jehovah's house and the king's house.
After I paid Hazael, he withdrew from Jerusalem.
I did not remember the loyal love Jehoiada had shown toward me, and I killed his son.
When the Syrians withdrew, they left me severely wounded, and my own servants killed me on my own bed.
They buried me in the City of David, but they did not bury me in the burial places of the kings.
Jehosheba kept me and my nurse concealed in an inner bedroom before I was hidden at Jehovah's house.
When they made me king, Jehoiada gave the chiefs the spears and circular shields that had belonged to David and were in Jehovah's house.
I asked Jehoiada why he had not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the sacred tax Moses ordered for the tent of the Testimony.
I said the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of the true God and used the holy things for the Baals.
Under my reign Jehoiada took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and put it next to the altar on the right as one enters Jehovah's house.
None of the money brought for my temple repairs was used to make basins of silver, extinguishers, bowls, trumpets, or any gold or silver article.
After my renovation finished, leftover money was used to make utensils of gold and silver for Jehovah's house.
Under my repairs they would not call for an accounting from the men who paid the workers, for they were trustworthy.
In my day the money for guilt offerings and sin offerings was not brought to Jehovah's house for the repairs; it belonged to the priests.
After Jehoiada died at 130 years of age, the princes of Judah came and bowed down to me, and I listened to them.
Jehovah kept sending prophets among us to bring us back, but we refused to listen.
God's spirit came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada, and he stood above my people.
Zechariah said that because we had abandoned Jehovah, he would abandon us.
As Zechariah was dying he said of me: “May Jehovah see to it and call you to account.”
My servants struck me down at the house of the Mound, on the way that goes down to Silla.
Jozacar the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer struck me and put me to death.
The conspirators against me were Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonitess and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith the Moabitess.
Although the Syrian army had a small number of men, Jehovah handed my very large army over to them.
I sent Hazael the holy offerings that my forefathers Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, the kings of Judah, had sanctified, as well as my own.
While Athaliah destroyed the entire royal line of the house of Judah, I alone of Ahaziah's sons survived, hidden with my nurse at Jehovah's house.
They buried Jehoiada, who had raised me, in the City of David along with the kings because he had done good.
I renovated Jehovah's house after Athaliah's sons had broken into it for the Baals.
Jehoshabeath of Jehoiada's household saved my life, yet at my order Jehoiada's son was stoned in the courtyard of Jehovah's house.
All the days of Jehoiada, while I did what was right, they offered burnt sacrifices regularly at Jehovah's house.
My servants conspired against me because I had shed the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest.
The princes of Judah who bowed down to me after Jehoiada's death were later done away with when the Syrian army invaded.
I paid Hazael from the treasuries of Jehovah's house so he would leave.
Jehovah handed Judah over to a small Syrian army during my reign because we had abandoned him.
I was the son of Jehoshaphat and became king in his place.
I reigned for eight years in Jerusalem.
I was 32 years old when I became king.
Ahab's daughter became my wife, and I walked in the way of the kings of Israel.
I kept doing what was bad in Jehovah's eyes.
My son Ahaziah became king in my place.
My father gave me the kingdom because I was the firstborn.
When I took control of the kingdom, I strengthened my position by killing all my brothers with the sword.
I also killed some of the princes of Israel when I strengthened my hold on the kingdom.
In my days Edom revolted against Judah and set up its own king.
I crossed over with my chariots, rose up by night, and defeated the Edomites who were surrounding me.
Libnah also revolted against me.
I made high places on the mountains of Judah and led Judah astray.
Jehovah afflicted me with an incurable disease in my intestines.
After two full years my intestines came out because of the disease, and I died while suffering severely.
They buried me in the City of David, but not in the burial places of the kings.
My brothers were Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah.
My father gave my brothers many gifts in silver and gold and fortified cities in Judah, but he gave the kingdom to me.
Elijah sent me a written message from Jehovah the God of David my forefather.
Elijah's message said I had not walked in the ways of my father Jehoshaphat or of King Asa of Judah.
Elijah's message said I had killed my own brothers, the household of my father, who were better than I.
Elijah warned that I would suffer a disease of my intestines until my intestines came out day after day.
Jehovah stirred up against me the Philistines and the Arabs who were near the Ethiopians.
Invaders carried off all the possessions found in the king's house, as well as my sons and my wives.
The only son left to me was Jehoahaz, my youngest son.
My people did not make a burning for me like the burning made for my forefathers.
No one regretted it when I died.
Matthew's genealogy says Jehoshaphat became father to me, and I became father to Uzziah.
Jehovah would not bring the house of David to ruin for the sake of his covenant with David, though I did what was bad in Jehovah's eyes.
Libnah revolted against me at the same time Edom did, because I had abandoned Jehovah the God of my forefathers.
After Philistines and Arabs carried off my wives and sons, Jehovah then afflicted me with the intestinal disease Elijah's letter had warned about.
Though invaders killed my older sons, the inhabitants of Jerusalem later made my youngest son Ahaziah king in my place.
My daughter Jehoshabeath was the wife of Jehoiada the priest.
My daughter Jehoshabeath, stole Joash away from among the sons of the king who were to be put to death by Athaliah.
I was laid to rest with my forefathers in the City of David, yet not in the burial places of the kings, and no one regretted my death.
I was a daughter of King Jehoram.
Ahaziah the king was my brother.
I was the wife of Jehoiada the priest.
I stole Jehoash from among the sons of the king who were to be put to death by Athaliah.
I concealed Jehoash and his nurse in an inner bedroom.
Jehoash remained with me, hidden at the house of Jehovah for six years while Athaliah ruled over the land.
I was the son of Asa and became king over Judah.
I walked in the way of my father Asa and did not deviate from it.
Jehovah was with me because I walked in the former ways of my forefather David and did not search for the Baals.
I searched for the God of my father and followed his commandment, not the practices of Israel.
My heart became bold in the ways of Jehovah, and I removed the high places and the sacred poles from Judah.
I made a marriage alliance with Ahab.
When Ahab asked if I would go with him to Ramoth-gilead, I said I was the same as he was, and my people the same as his people.
Before going up with Ahab, I asked him first to inquire for the word of Jehovah.
I asked if there was not a prophet of Jehovah so we could also inquire through him.
When Syrian chariot commanders mistook me for the king of Israel, I cried for help, and Jehovah helped me.
When Moabites and Ammonites came against me, I became afraid and resolved to search for Jehovah.
I proclaimed a fast for all Judah.
I told Judah we were powerless before the large crowd, but our eyes were toward Jehovah.
I stood in Jehovah's house before the new courtyard and prayed as Judah assembled.
My people and I carried off spoil for three days.
My ships to go for gold were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
After I was laid to rest, my son Jehoram became king in my place.
I became king over Judah in the fourth year of King Ahab of Israel.
I was 35 years old when I became king, and I reigned for 25 years in Jerusalem.
My mother's name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
I stationed military forces in all the fortified cities of Judah.
I put garrisons in Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa my father had captured.
All Judah continued to give gifts to me, and I had riches and glory in abundance.
In the third year of my reign I sent princes, Levites, and priests to teach in the cities of Judah.
My teachers taught among the people, taking with them the book of Jehovah's Law.
The dread of Jehovah came upon the kingdoms surrounding Judah, and they did not fight against me.
The Philistines brought me gifts and money as tribute.
The Arabs brought me 7,700 rams and 7,700 male goats.
I continued building fortified places and storage cities in Judah.
Ahab sacrificed sheep and cattle in abundance for me when I went down to him at Samaria.
When Ahab said he hated Micaiah, I said he should not say such a thing.
Ahab and I sat on our thrones in royal attire at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria.
Ahab told me he would disguise himself and go into battle, but I should put on my royal attire.
Jehu asked me if it was the wicked I should be helping and those who hate Jehovah I should love.
Jehu said that nevertheless good things had been found in me, because I cleared out the sacred poles.
Jehu said I had prepared my heart to search for the true God.
I went out among the people from Beer-sheba to the mountainous region of Ephraim to bring them back to Jehovah.
I appointed judges throughout the land in all the fortified cities of Judah.
I told the judges they did not judge for man but for Jehovah.
I said that with Jehovah our God there is no injustice, no partiality, no bribe-taking.
Jahaziel said the battle was not ours but God's, and we would not need to fight.
I bowed low with my face to the ground, and all Judah fell down before Jehovah to worship.
Going out to the wilderness of Tekoa, I told Judah to put faith in Jehovah and in his prophets.
After consulting with the people, I appointed singers to go out ahead of the armed men praising Jehovah.
On the fourth day we congregated at the Valley of Beracah, for there we praised Jehovah.
I kept peaceful relations with the king of Israel.
I cleared out of the land the rest of the male temple prostitutes left over from the days of Asa my father.
When Ahaziah son of Ahab asked that his servants go with mine in the ships, I did not consent.
When Jehoram of Israel asked me to go to war against Moab, I said I would go, for I was the same as he was.
When the three kings ran out of water, I asked if there was no prophet of Jehovah through whom we might inquire.
Elisha said that if he did not have regard for me, he would not look at the king of Israel or take notice of him.
I strengthened my position over Israel when I became king.
I did what was right in Jehovah's eyes, but the high places were not removed in my day.
In my day there was no king in Edom; a deputy was acting as king.
I made Tarshish ships to go to Ophir for gold.
I made an alliance with King Ahaziah of Israel, who acted wickedly, to make ships to go to Tarshish.
Eliezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah said that because I had made an alliance with Ahaziah, Jehovah would destroy my works.
We went up against Moab by the way of the wilderness of Edom.
I gave my other sons many gifts in silver and gold and fortified cities in Judah.
I gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.
In Jerusalem I also appointed Levites, priests, and heads of paternal houses to serve as judges for Jehovah.
I told the judges Amariah the chief priest was over them for every matter of Jehovah.
I told the judges Zebadiah the son of Ishmael was over them for every matter pertaining to the king.
When my people came to the watchtower of the wilderness, they saw the invaders' carcasses fallen to the ground; there were no survivors.
Matthew's genealogy says Asa became father to me, and I became father to Jehoram.
My history from beginning to end was written among the words of Jehu the son of Hanani.
I told Jehovah that Ammon, Moab, and the mountainous region of Seir were ones he had not allowed Israel to invade when they came out of Egypt.
I walked boldly against Baal worship and taught Jehovah's Law in Judah.
I also bound myself to Ahab's house by marriage alliance.
I insisted on hearing a prophet of Jehovah before Ramoth-gilead.
I still went into battle in royal attire while Ahab disguised himself.
Jehu rebuked me for helping the wicked after Ramoth-gilead.
After Jehu rebuked me for helping the wicked at Ramoth-gilead, I appointed judges and again brought the people back to Jehovah.
Facing Ammon, Moab, and Seir, I confessed powerlessness.
Jehovah fought for me while singers went ahead of the army.
After Jehovah gave me rest on every side, I still partnered with wicked Ahaziah to build ships.
Twice I answered northern kings with nearly the same pledge of shared identity before joining their wars.
I cleared sacred poles and male temple prostitutes from Judah.
I was anointed as king over Israel at Ramoth-gilead.
I was an army chief when I was anointed king.
A watchman recognized my approach because I drive like a madman.
I shot Jehoram between the shoulders, and the arrow came out through his heart.
I ordered Jezebel thrown down from a window.
I trampled Jezebel underfoot.
I annihilated Baal out of Israel.
I reigned over Israel for 28 years in Samaria.
Jehovah promised that four generations of my sons would sit on Israel's throne.
I conspired against Jehoram and became king in his place.
I had Jehoram's body thrown into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite.
I struck down all who were left of Ahab's house.
My fellow officers blew the horn and proclaimed that I had become king.
I was buried in Samaria.
My son Jehoahaz became king in my place.
I was the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi.
A prophet's attendant poured oil on my head.
He said Jehovah had anointed me king over Jehovah's people, over Israel.
When horsemen asked if I was coming in peace, I said, “What do you have to do with 'peace'?”
I told the horsemen, “Fall in behind me!”
I told Jehoram there could be no peace while Jezebel's prostitution continued.
I told Jehoram there could be no peace while Jezebel's many sorceries continued.
Jezebel looked down from a window and asked me if it had gone well with Zimri, the killer of his lord.
Looking up to Jezebel's window, I asked, “Who is on my side? Who?”
I wrote letters to Samaria about Ahab's 70 sons.
I later demanded that the heads of Ahab's sons be brought to me at Jezreel.
I encountered Jehonadab the son of Rechab.
I asked Jehonadab if his heart was fully with me.
I pulled Jehonadab up into my chariot.
I told Jehonadab to come along and see my toleration of no rivalry toward Jehovah.
I told the people that Ahab had worshipped Baal a little, but I would worship him much more.
I tore down the house of Baal and turned it into latrines.
I did not turn away from the golden calves Jeroboam set in Bethel and in Dan.
Jehovah told Elijah to anoint me as king over Israel.
Jehoram and Ahaziah came out to meet me in Naboth's plot of land.
When my lord's servants asked why the crazy man had come, I said they knew that sort of man and his talk.
After I was proclaimed king, I said no one should escape from the city to report it in Jezreel.
I told Bidkar my adjutant to remember that we had ridden together behind Ahab.
I recalled Jehovah's pronouncement against Ahab over Naboth's blood.
I pursued Ahaziah of Judah as he fled.
I ordered that Ahaziah also be struck down.
After Jezebel was thrown down, I went in and ate and drank.
I said to take care of that accursed woman and bury her, for she was a king's daughter.
When they went to bury Jezebel for me, only her skull, feet, and the palms of her hands were found.
I said Jezebel's end fulfilled Jehovah's word spoken through Elijah the Tishbite.
I had the heads of Ahab's sons put in two heaps at the city gate.
I asked the people who had struck down all of these.
On the way to Samaria I captured 42 brothers of Ahaziah.
I slaughtered Ahaziah's brothers at the cistern of the binding house of the shepherds.
With Jehonadab I went into Baal's house.
I had Baal's worshippers searched so that no worshippers of Jehovah were among them.
I stationed 80 men outside Baal's house.
I said that if any man I put into their hands escaped, it would be their life for his.
I did not take care to walk in the Law of Jehovah with all my heart.
In my days Jehovah started to cut off Israel piece by piece.
In my days Hazael kept attacking Israel's territory east of the Jordan, all the land of Gilead.
I was anointed to strike down Ahab's house.
I was to avenge the blood of Jehovah's servants who died at Jezebel's hands.
Through Hosea, Jehovah later said he would hold an accounting against my house for the bloodshed of Jezreel.
Because I did what was right regarding Ahab's house, Jehovah promised four generations of my sons the throne.
Jehovah's word about four generations of my sons was fulfilled when Zechariah sat as king.
Jehovah told Elijah that anyone escaping from Hazael's sword I would put to death.
Jehovah said anyone escaping from my sword, Elisha would put to death.
Elisha sent the messenger who anointed me.
I fulfilled Jehovah's word against Jezebel in Jezreel's plot of land.
I finished annihilating Ahab's house in Samaria according to the word Jehovah had spoken to Elijah.
I was laid to rest in Samaria after Hazael had cut Israel down east of the Jordan.
I cast Jehoram into Naboth's plot because of Jehovah's word against Ahab.
I later stood before the people of Jezreel with the heads of Ahab's sons heaped at the city gate.
Chronicles says God brought about Ahaziah's downfall by his coming to Jehoram to meet me.
Ahaziah went out to meet me, whom Jehovah had anointed to do away with Ahab's house.
When I executed judgment on Ahab's house, I also killed princes of Judah.
I killed the sons of Ahaziah's brothers who were Ahaziah's ministers.
I was the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah.
My mother's name was Zeruah, a widow.
I was a servant of Solomon.
Ahijah the Shilonite ripped a new garment into 12 pieces and told me to take ten.
Jehovah said he would give me ten tribes.
Solomon tried to put me to death, so I fled to Egypt, to Shishak the king of Egypt.
After Solomon's death, all Israel summoned me and made me king over all Israel.
I built up Shechem in the mountainous region of Ephraim and lived there.
I made two golden calves and told the people it was too much for them to go up to Jerusalem.
I said, “Here is your God, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”
I placed one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan.
My calves caused the people to sin, and they went as far as Dan to worship the one there.
I appointed priests from the people in general, those who were not Levites.
While I stood by the altar at Bethel to make sacrificial smoke, a man of God from Judah called out against the altar.
When I stretched out my hand and said “Seize him!” my hand dried up, and I could not draw it back.
After the man of God from Judah prayed, my hand was restored to its former condition.
Ahijah said I had done worse than all who were prior to me and had made another god and metal images.
Ahijah said Jehovah would make a clean sweep of my house.
My son Nadab became king in my place.
Solomon saw that I was a capable man and a hard worker, so he made me overseer over all the compulsory service of the house of Joseph.
Ahijah found me on the road when I went out from Jerusalem; he and I were alone in a field.
Jehovah said that if I obeyed and walked in his ways like David, he would build me a lasting house.
I remained in Egypt until Solomon's death.
With all the congregation of Israel I asked Rehoboam to lighten the heavy yoke Solomon had put on us.
When Rehoboam refused to listen to us, Israel revolted against the house of David.
None of the people followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah, and they made me king.
From Shechem I went out and built up Penuel.
I said in my heart that if the people kept going up to Jerusalem, they would kill me and return to Rehoboam.
I established a festival in the eighth month, on the 15th day, like the festival in Judah.
I asked a man of God to beg for Jehovah's favor so my hand might be restored.
I invited the man of God to come home with me and take food and receive a gift, but he refused.
I kept appointing priests for the high places from the people in general.
When my son Abijah fell sick, I told my wife to disguise herself and go to Ahijah at Shiloh.
I told my wife to take ten loaves, sprinkled cakes, and a flask of honey.
Ahijah said anyone belonging to me who died in the city, the dogs would eat.
Only my sick child would be buried, because in him alone Jehovah had found something good.
As my wife came to the threshold of the house in Tirzah, my son died.
I reigned for 22 years.
There was constant warfare between Rehoboam and me.
I drew up in battle formation against Abijah with 800,000 trained mighty warriors.
I dispatched an ambush to come from behind Judah.
Jehovah's priests, the descendants of Aaron, and the Levites left their pastures and property and came to Judah because I and my sons had dismissed them from serving as priests.
I appointed my own priests for the high places, for the goat-shaped demons, and for the calves I had made.
I began to rebel against Solomon after he built the Mound and closed up the gap of the City of David.
Ahijah told me one tribe would remain for Solomon's son for David's sake and for Jerusalem.
I made houses of worship on the high places.
The man of God told me a son named Josiah would be born to the house of David and would sacrifice the priests of the high places on that altar.
Before me the altar was ripped apart and the ashes spilled out according to the sign the man of God had given.
This sin on the part of my household led to their destruction and annihilation from the face of the earth.
Ahijah said Jehovah had raised me up from among the people to make me a leader over Israel.
Ahijah said Jehovah ripped the kingdom from David's house and gave it to me.
Ahijah said Jehovah would raise up a king who would do away with my house.
