Jehovah struck Israel and would abandon them because of the sins I committed and caused Israel to commit.
Abijah captured Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephrain with their dependent towns from me.
I never regained my power during Abijah's time; then Jehovah struck me down and I died.
Later kings of Israel kept walking in my way, the way of the man who had caused Israel to sin.
Baasha struck down all my house according to Jehovah's word spoken through Ahijah.
Jehovah offered me a lasting house like David's if I obeyed.
Instead I feared losing the people and made calves so they would not go up to Jerusalem.
Ahijah first gave me ten pieces of a garment as kingship promise.
Ahijah the prophet announced a clean sweep of my house for turning my back on Jehovah.
After my hand was restored, I still would not turn from appointing unlawful priests.
I sent my wife in disguise to the prophet who had once promised me the kingdom.
Ahijah recognized her and announced our child's death and our house's end.
Against Abijah I set an ambush behind Judah, but God defeated me.
Scripture keeps naming later northern sin as walking in my way, the way of the man who caused Israel to sin with the calves.
I was the daughter of Ethbaal, the king of the Sidonians.
Ahab took me as wife.
Four hundred prophets of the sacred pole were eating at my table.
I was doing away with Jehovah's prophets.
After Ahab told me all that Elijah had done to the prophets of Baal, I sent a messenger to Elijah.
I swore that by this time tomorrow I would make Elijah's life the same as the life of one of those prophets of Baal that he killed.
When Ahab was sullen over Naboth's vineyard, I asked why he was so sad that he refused to eat.
I told Ahab he was the one ruling as king over Israel, and that I would give him Naboth's vineyard.
I wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal.
In my letters I ordered that Naboth be accused of cursing God and the king, then stoned to death.
When I heard Naboth had been stoned, I told Ahab to get up and take possession of the vineyard.
Jehovah said the dogs would eat me up in the plot of land of Jezreel.
Scripture says Ahab was egged on by me his wife.
When Jehu came to Jezreel, I painted my eyes with black paint and adorned my head and looked down through the window.
From a window in Jezreel, I asked Jehu if it had gone well with Zimri, the killer of his lord.
Court officials threw me down, and Jehu trampled me.
Dogs left of me only my skull, my feet, and the palms of my hands.
Through marriage to me, Ahab began to serve Baal and to bow down to him.
Prophets of Baal and of the sacred pole who ate at my table were summoned to Mount Carmel.
While I was killing Jehovah's prophets, Obadiah hid 100 of them by groups of 50 in a cave.
After Carmel, Ahab told me everything Elijah had done.
Elijah ran for his life because of my threat.
I told Ahab to get up, eat something, and let his heart be cheerful.
I sent letters to the elders and nobles who lived in Naboth's city, ordering them to proclaim a fast and have Naboth sit at the head of the people.
The elders and nobles in Naboth's city did just as was written in the letters I sent.
Elders and nobles sent word to me that Naboth had been stoned to death.
Jehovah said dogs would eat me in the plot of land of Jezreel, and no one would bury me.
Jehu told my son that there could be no peace while there was my prostitution and my many sorceries.
Jehu said to take care of this accursed woman and bury her, for I was the daughter of a king.
My dead body was to become as manure on the surface of the field in Jezreel's plot.
No one would even recognize my remains.
My son Ahaziah became king after Ahab.
My son Jehoram also reigned over Israel.
Jehoram clung to sins less than his father or me, for he removed Baal's sacred pillar.
Ahab did more to offend Jehovah than all prior kings of Israel after taking me as wife and serving Baal.
Elijah named the 400 prophets of the sacred pole as those eating at my table when he summoned Israel to Carmel.
Jehovah's judgment on Ahab's house included a specific sentence against me by name.
Jehu was anointed to avenge the blood of Jehovah's servants who died at my hands.
After I was thrown down, some of my blood splattered on the wall and on the horses.
My daughter Athaliah became wife to Jehoram of Judah.
Through my daughter, that house of Judah walked in the way of Ahab.
Jehu said my death fulfilled Jehovah's word through Elijah.
I fed hundreds of Baal and sacred-pole prophets from my table.
I tried to wipe out Jehovah's prophets; Obadiah's hidden hundred survived my purge.
After Elijah slaughtered the prophets of Baal, I answered with a next-day death oath.
Then I told Ahab to take possession of Naboth's vineyard.
Jehu refused peace because of my prostitution and sorceries.
Jehu ordered me thrown from the window of Jezreel.
My Sidonian royal birth and marriage pulled Israel into Baal worship.
Through my daughter Athaliah, the influence of Ahab's house reached Judah's royal family.
I was the son of Amon, and I became king of Judah.
I became king at eight years of age and reigned for 31 years in Jerusalem.
I did what was right in Jehovah's eyes and walked in all the ways of David my forefather.
I did not deviate to the right or to the left.
While my servants were repairing Jehovah's house, Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the Law.
As soon as I heard the words of the book of the Law, I ripped my garments apart.
I sent men to inquire of Jehovah, and they went to Huldah the prophetess.
I stood by the pillar and made a covenant before Jehovah to follow him with all my heart and with all my soul.
I held a Passover to Jehovah in Jerusalem in the 18th year of my reign.
There was no king like me who returned to Jehovah with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength, according to all the Law of Moses.
Nor did anyone like me rise up after me.
Pharaoh Nechoh's archers mortally wounded me at Megiddo.
My servants transported my dead body in a chariot from Megiddo and buried me in Jerusalem.
The people of the land took my son Jehoahaz and made him king in my place.
Matthew's genealogy says Amon became father to me, and I became father to Jeconiah and to his brothers at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
Jeremiah chanted over me, and singers kept singing about me in their dirges.
My mother's name was Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath.
After Amon's servants killed him, the people of the land struck down the conspirators and made me king.
In the 18th year of my reign I sent Shaphan the secretary to the house of Jehovah about repairing the damage.
Shaphan the secretary read the book of the Law before me after Hilkiah gave it to him.
I ordered Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah to inquire of Jehovah in my behalf and in behalf of all Judah.
Huldah said Jehovah would gather me to my ancestors and I would be laid in my grave in peace.
Huldah said my eyes would not see the coming calamity.
I went up to Jehovah's house and read in the people's hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found.
I ordered that all the utensils made for Baal, for the sacred pole, and for all the army of the heavens be brought out of Jehovah's temple.
I brought the sacred pole out from Jehovah's house to the Kidron Valley and burned it.
I ground the sacred pole to dust and scattered its dust on the graves of the common people.
I made Topheth in the Valley of the Sons of Hinnom unfit for worship so no one could make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.
I tore down the altar and high place at Bethel that Jeroboam the son of Nebat had made.
I burned human bones on Bethel's altar, making it unfit for worship.
No Passover like mine had been held since the days when the judges judged Israel.
I cleared out the spirit mediums, the fortune-tellers, the teraphim statues, and the disgusting idols from Judah and Jerusalem.
I contributed 30,000 male lambs and young male goats for the Passover sacrifices from the king's own property.
I also contributed 3,000 cattle for the Passover from the king's own property.
Archers shot me in the Plain of Megiddo, and I told my servants I was severely wounded.
My servants took me out of the chariot, had me ride in my second war chariot, and brought me to Jerusalem, where I died.
The word of Jehovah came to Jeremiah in the 13th year of my reign.
In the 8th year of my reign, while I was still a boy, I started to search for the God of David my forefather.
In the 12th year of my reign I started to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the sacred poles, the graven images, and the metal statues.
I burned the bones of priests on their altars as I cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
I tore down altars and crushed sacred poles and graven images in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and clear to Naphtali.
I put out of business the foreign-god priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed.
I put out of business those making sacrificial smoke to Baal, to the sun, to the moon, to the constellations of the zodiac, and to all the army of the heavens.
I tore down the houses of the male temple prostitutes that were in the house of Jehovah, where women were weaving tent shrines for the sacred pole.
I made the high places unfit for worship from Geba to Beer-sheba.
I prohibited the horses dedicated to the sun from entering Jehovah's house, and I burned the chariots of the sun.
I tore down the altars on the roof of Ahaz's upper chamber.
I tore down the altars Manasseh had set up in two courtyards of Jehovah's house.
I made unfit for worship the high places south of the Mount of Ruination that Solomon had built to Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom.
When I saw the grave of the man of the true God from Judah who foretold what I did at Bethel, I said to leave his bones undisturbed.
I also left undisturbed the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
I removed the houses of worship on the high places in the cities of Samaria.
I sacrificed the priests of the high places on their altars in the cities of Samaria.
I told the Levites to put the holy Ark in the house Solomon built; they were no longer to carry it on their shoulders.
There had never been a Passover like mine in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet.
Pharaoh Nechoh made my son Eliakim king in my place and changed his name to Jehoiakim.
Long before I was born, a man of the true God named me and said I would sacrifice the priests of the high places on Bethel's altar.
The men I sent found Huldah the prophetess dwelling in the Second Quarter of Jerusalem.
Even after my reforms, Jehovah did not turn away from his burning anger against Judah because of all the offensive things Manasseh had done.
When Nechoh came up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates, I went out against him.
Nechoh sent word that God was with him and told me to refrain from opposing God, but I would not listen.
I disguised myself to fight against Nechoh in the Plain of Megiddo.
Chronicles lists my sons as Johanan the firstborn, Jehoiakim the second, Zedekiah the third, and Shallum the fourth.
Jehovah's word concerning Shallum my son said he was reigning instead of me and would die in the land of his exile without returning.
A prophet later told Jehoiakim that I upheld justice and righteousness and defended the legal claim of the afflicted one and the poor one.
Zephaniah son of Cushi received Jehovah's word in my days.
In my days Jehovah spoke to Jeremiah about what unfaithful Israel had done and about treacherous Judah.
Throughout my lifetime the people did not deviate from following Jehovah the God of their forefathers after I made everyone in Israel serve him.
I was the son of Uzziah and became king over Judah.
I was 25 years old when I became king.
I reigned for 16 years in Jerusalem.
I built the upper gate of the house of Jehovah.
My son Ahaz became king in my place.
Matthew's genealogy says Uzziah became father to me, and I became father to Ahaz.
My mother was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.
I did what was right just as my father Uzziah had done.
The high places were not removed in my days, and the people were still sacrificing and making sacrificial smoke on them.
I did much building on the wall of Ophel.
I built cities in the mountainous region of Judah.
I built fortified places and towers in the wooded areas.
I waged war against the king of the Ammonites and prevailed.
The Ammonites gave me 100 silver talents in that year.
The Ammonites also gave me 10,000 cor measures of wheat and 10,000 of barley.
The Ammonites paid me that tribute in the second and third years as well.
I kept growing strong, for I established my ways before Jehovah my God.
I became king in the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah.
I was laid to rest with my forefathers and buried in the City of David.
Isaiah's vision came in the days of Uzziah, me, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hosea's word from Jehovah came in the days of Uzziah, me, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
Micah's word of Jehovah came in the days of me, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
I did what was right like my father Uzziah, except that I did not invade the temple of Jehovah.
The people were still acting ruinously in my days.
In my days Jehovah began sending Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah against Judah.
Genealogies were enrolled in my days as king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.
While my father stayed in a separate house as a leper, excluded from Jehovah's house, I judged the people of the land.
I walked Uzziah's right path without repeating his invasion of Jehovah's temple.
I grew strong by establishing my ways before Jehovah, yet the high places remained and the people acted ruinously.
I was the son of Hezekiah, and I became king of Judah.
I became king at 12 years of age and reigned for 55 years in Jerusalem.
I did what was bad in Jehovah's eyes, following the detestable practices of the nations.
I rebuilt the high places that my father Hezekiah had destroyed.
I set up altars to Baal.
I made a sacred pole, just as Ahab the king of Israel had done.
I bowed down to all the army of the heavens and served them.
I built altars in the house of Jehovah.
I made my own son pass through the fire.
I shed innocent blood in very great quantity until I had filled Jerusalem from one end to the other.
The army chiefs of the king of Assyria captured me with hooks.
They bound me with two copper fetters and took me to Babylon.
Jehovah restored me to Jerusalem to my kingship.
I came to know that Jehovah is the true God.
My son Amon became king in my place.
Matthew's genealogy says Hezekiah became father to me, and I became father to Amon.
My mother's name was Hephzibah.
I built altars to all the army of the heavens in two courtyards of the house of Jehovah.
I practiced magic and looked for omens.
I appointed spirit mediums and fortune-tellers.
I kept leading them astray, causing them to do greater evil than the nations Jehovah had annihilated.
I made my own sons pass through the fire in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom.
I used divination and practiced sorcery.
In my distress, I begged Jehovah my God for favor.
I kept humbling myself greatly before the God of my forefathers.
I kept praying to Jehovah, and he was moved by my entreaty and heard my request for favor.
I removed the foreign gods and the idol image from the house of Jehovah.
I prepared the altar of Jehovah and began to offer up communion sacrifices and thanksgiving sacrifices on it.
I told Judah to serve Jehovah the God of Israel.
I was buried in the garden of my house, in the garden of Uzza.
I set up altars to the Baals and made sacred poles.
Jehovah's prophets said I had acted more wickedly than all the Amorites before me.
Jehovah's prophets said I had made Judah sin with my disgusting idols.
Jehovah said because of me he was bringing a disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that would make both ears of anyone who heard about it tingle.
Jehovah said because of my sins he would stretch out on Jerusalem the measuring line applied to Samaria and the leveling tool applied to the house of Ahab.
Jehovah said because of me he would wipe Jerusalem clean, just as one wipes a bowl clean, wiping it and turning it upside down.
Jehovah kept speaking to me and my people, but we paid no attention.
I built an outer wall for the City of David west of Gihon in the valley and as far as the Fish Gate.
I continued that wall around to Ophel and made it very high.
I appointed army chiefs in all the fortified cities in Judah.
I had all the altars I had built in the mountain of Jehovah's house and in Jerusalem thrown outside the city.
After my reforms, the people were still sacrificing on the high places, although only to Jehovah their God.
I did on a grand scale what was bad in Jehovah's eyes, to offend him.
My prayer to my God and the words of the visionaries who spoke to me are recorded in the history of the kings of Israel.
Josiah tore down the altars I had set up in two courtyards of the house of Jehovah.
Even after Josiah's reforms, Jehovah did not turn away from his burning anger against Judah because of all the offensive things I had done.
Later Scripture says Judah was removed from Jehovah's sight because of all the sins I had committed.
Later Scripture also cites the innocent blood I had shed, for I had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood and Jehovah was not willing to forgive.
Jehovah said through Jeremiah that he would make them an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of what I did in Jerusalem.
My son Amon did not humble himself before Jehovah as I his father had humbled myself.
Amon sacrificed to all the graven images that I had made, and he kept serving them.
After condemning my wickedness, Jehovah said he would forsake the remnant of his inheritance and give them into the hand of their enemies.
The words of my visionaries also record the locations where I built high places and set up the sacred poles and the graven images before I humbled myself.
After Assyria took me to Babylon in copper fetters, Jehovah heard my prayer and restored my kingship in Jerusalem.
I put a carved sacred-pole image into the house about which Jehovah had told David and Solomon he would permanently put his name.
I kept leading Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray, causing them to do worse than the nations Jehovah had annihilated.
The king of Israel hated me because I did not prophesy good things concerning him, only bad.
Jehoshaphat asked for a prophet of Jehovah, and I was the one still available to inquire through.
I said that as surely as Jehovah is living, whatever Jehovah says to me is what I will speak.
I saw all the Israelites scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd.
I said Jehovah had declared calamity for the king of Israel.
I was put in prison and fed with a reduced allowance of bread and water.
I said that if the king of Israel returned in peace, Jehovah had not spoken with me.
I was the son of Imlah.
A court official was told to bring me quickly.
The messenger urged me to speak favorably, like the other prophets.
When asked about war at Ramoth-gilead, I first said to go up and be successful.
The king of Israel put me under oath not to speak anything but the truth in Jehovah's name.
I said Jehovah declared those scattered ones had no master and should each go back to his house in peace.
I saw Jehovah sitting on his throne.
I saw all the army of the heavens standing by him, to his right and to his left.
I said Jehovah had put a deceptive spirit in the mouth of all those prophets.
Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah struck me on the cheek.
I was turned over to Amon the chief of the city and to Joash the king's son.
About 400 prophets were already prophesying success before I was brought.
The kings were sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria when I was brought to speak.
I reported that a spirit stood before Jehovah and offered to fool Ahab so he would go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead.
I reported that the spirit said he would become a deceptive spirit in the mouth of all Ahab's prophets.
I told Zedekiah he would see which way on the day he entered the innermost room to hide.
After my warning I added, “Take note, all you peoples.”
I first echoed the favorable word, then under oath revealed the sheep-without-shepherd vision.
I reported a heavenly council where Jehovah allowed a deceptive spirit to succeed in Ahab's prophets' mouths.
My prison food was to last until the king of Israel returned in peace; he fell at Ramoth-gilead instead.
Alone against a unanimous favorable chorus, I told all the peoples to take note of my word.
I was the army chief of the king of Syria.
I was a mighty warrior, although I was a leper.
Through me Jehovah had given victory to Syria.
A little girl from Israel, servant to my wife, spoke of a prophet in Samaria.
Elisha's messenger told me to wash seven times in the Jordan.
I plunged into the Jordan seven times and became clean.
My flesh was restored like the flesh of a little boy.
I said there is no God anywhere in all the earth but in Israel.
I was a prominent man held in esteem by my lord.
I took ten talents of silver, 6,000 pieces of gold, and ten changes of garments.
I brought the king of Syria's letter to the king of Israel.
I came with horses and war chariots and stood at the entrance of Elisha's house.
I became indignant when Elisha only sent a messenger.
I had said to myself that he would call on Jehovah and move his hand over the leprosy.
I said the Abanah and the Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, were better than all the waters of Israel.
I turned and went away in a rage.
My servants asked whether I would have done something extraordinary if Elisha had required it.
I went back to the man of the true God with all my entourage.
I asked Elisha to accept a gift, but he kept refusing.
I asked for two mule-loads of soil from that land.
I said I would no longer offer a burnt offering or a sacrifice to any gods other than Jehovah.
Jesus later said that of many lepers in Israel in Elisha's time, only I the Syrian was cleansed.
On a raid my people had taken captive the little girl who served my wife.
When Gehazi ran after me, I got down from my chariot to meet him.
I urged Gehazi and gave him two talents of silver and two changes of garments.
I asked that Jehovah forgive me when I bow at the house of Rimmon as my lord leans on my arm.
Elisha told me, “Go in peace.”
I almost walked away unclean because Jordan seemed lesser than the rivers of Damascus.
After I was cleansed, I asked for Israelite soil so I could sacrifice only to Jehovah.
I pledged exclusive offerings to Jehovah while still asking pardon for bowing in Rimmon's house.
After Elisha refused my gift, his attendant chased me and took silver and garments in his master's name.
I was over Ahab's household.
I greatly feared Jehovah.
When Jezebel was doing away with Jehovah's prophets, I hid 100 of them.
I hid Jehovah's prophets, 50 to a cave.
I supplied those prophets with bread and water.
Ahab told me to search the springs and valleys for grass for the horses and mules.
Along the road I recognized Elijah and fell facedown.
Ahab and I divided the land between ourselves, each going alone by a different way.
I asked Elijah, “Is this you, my lord Elijah?”
Elijah told me to go and tell my lord that Elijah is here.
I feared Ahab would put me to death if Elijah could not be found.
I said I had feared Jehovah from my youth.
I went off to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
I reminded Elijah how I had hidden 100 prophets when Jezebel was killing them.
I said there was not a nation or kingdom where my lord had not sent to look for Elijah.
I said that after they claimed Elijah was not there, Ahab made the kingdom and the nation swear they could not find him.
I feared that when I left, the spirit of Jehovah would carry Elijah away to a place I would not know.
I asked what sin I had committed that Elijah would hand me over to Ahab to put me to death.
Elijah swore to me that as surely as Jehovah of armies whom he serves is living, he would present himself to Ahab that day.
I served in Ahab's household while secretly keeping Jehovah's prophets alive with bread and water.
In the famine Elijah had announced, I searched for grass to keep Ahab's animals alive.
After Ahab's long hunt for Elijah through nations and oaths, I was told to announce that Elijah is here.
Despite fearing Ahab's wrath, I went and delivered Elijah's message to the king.
I was chief of the army when all Israel made me king.
I bought the mountain of Samaria and built a city on it.
I named the city I built Samaria, after Shemer.
My son Ahab became king in my place.
I was buried in Samaria.
I was king over Israel.
Israel made me king in the camp after hearing Zimri had struck down King Elah.
I went up from Gibbethon with all Israel and laid siege to Tirzah.
I reigned for 12 years over Israel.
I reigned for six years in Tirzah.
I bought the mountain of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver.
I kept doing what was bad in Jehovah's eyes.
I walked in all the ways of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
One part of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath against me.
The people following me prevailed, Tibni died, and I became king.
I became king in the 31st year of King Asa of Judah.
I was worse than all who were prior to me.
By my ways Israel offended Jehovah with their worthless idols.
When Tirzah fell to me, Zimri burned the king's house down over himself.
My mighty exploits are written in the book of the history of the times of the kings of Israel.
Generations later Jehovah said Israel was still observing my statutes.
Athaliah my granddaughter ruled in Judah.
Ben-hadad said his father had taken cities from me.
After my 12 years, Ahab began to reign in the 38th year of Asa.
I was the son of Solomon and became king.
All Israel came to Shechem to make me king.
I rejected the older men's advice and followed the young men who grew up with me.
I told the people I would add to their yoke.
Ten tribes revolted, and I kept reigning over those in the cities of Judah.
I fled to Jerusalem after Israel stoned Adoram.
In my fifth year Shishak of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
Shishak took from me the gold shields Solomon had made.
I made copper shields to replace the gold ones.
My son Abijah became king in my place.
Matthew's genealogy says Solomon became father to me, and I became father to Abijah.
My mother's name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
I was 41 years old when I became king.
I reigned for 17 years in Jerusalem.
The people asked me to lighten Solomon's harsh yoke.
I told them to return in three days.
The older men told me to become a servant to the people and give a favorable answer.
I said my little finger would be thicker than my father's hips.
I said my father punished with whips, but I would punish with scourges.
I sent Adoram, who was over those conscripted for forced labor.
I congregated 180,000 trained warriors of Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel.
Through Shemaiah, Jehovah told us not to fight our brothers.
I built fortified cities in Judah.
Priests and Levites from all Israel took their stand with me.
For three years they strengthened Judah and supported me.
There was constant warfare between me and Jeroboam.
I was buried in my city.
I answered the people harshly.
I did not listen to the people's request to lighten their yoke, for this turn of events was caused by Jehovah.
In my case Jehovah carried out the word he had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam.
After I was firmly established and strong, I abandoned the Law of Jehovah.
Shemaiah said Jehovah had abandoned us to Shishak because we abandoned him.
The princes and I humbled ourselves and said, “Jehovah is righteous.”
Because I humbled myself, Jehovah's anger turned away and he did not destroy us completely.
I loved Maacah the granddaughter of Absalom more than all my other wives and concubines.
I took 18 wives and 60 concubines.
I became father to 28 sons and 60 daughters.
I appointed Abijah son of Maacah as head among his brothers, intending to make him king.
I did what was bad, for I had not resolved in my heart to search for Jehovah.
I reinforced fortified places and supplied them with food, oil, and wine.
Those from all the tribes of Israel who set their heart on seeking Jehovah came to Jerusalem with the Levites to support me.
For three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon while supporting me.
I married Mahalath, daughter of David's son Jerimoth and of Abihail daughter of Jesse's son Eliab.
I sent some of my sons to the fortified cities with abundant provisions.
Whenever I came to Jehovah's house, the guards carried the copper shields.
My history is written among the words of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the visionary.
Shishak brought Libyans, Sukkiim, and Ethiopians with him against me in Judah.
Only the tribe of Judah followed my house of David when Israel made Jeroboam king.
I was a prominent woman of Shunem.
I constrained Elisha to eat bread whenever he passed by.
I had a small roof room made for Elisha.
Elisha told me that at that time next year I would be embracing a son.
My son died, and Elisha restored him to life.
I went to Elisha at Mount Carmel when my son died.
I told my husband that the man who kept passing our way was a holy man of God.
I had Elisha's room furnished with a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand.
When Elisha offered to speak to the king of Israel or the chief of the army for me, I said I was dwelling among my own people.
I had no son, and my husband was old.
I told Elisha not to tell lies to his maidservant about a son.
I became pregnant and gave birth to a son just as Elisha had spoken.
My boy cried out, “My head! My head!” while with his father among the reapers.
After my son died, I laid him on the bed of the man of God and shut the door of the room.
Elisha told me to live as a foreigner wherever I could because Jehovah had declared a famine for seven years.
I sojourned in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
I appealed to the king of Israel for my house and my field.
I asked my husband for one of the servants and a donkey so I could go quickly to the man of God.
My husband asked why I was going to him that day, since it was not a new moon or a Sabbath.
I told my husband, “It is all right.”
I saddled the donkey and told my attendant not to slow down for me unless I said so.
When Gehazi asked whether I, my husband, and the child were well, I answered, “It is all right.”
At the mountain I grabbed hold of Elisha's feet.
Gehazi came near to push me away from Elisha.
I asked Elisha whether I had asked for a son from him.
I said as surely as Jehovah is living and as surely as Elisha was living, I would not leave him.
After Elisha restored my son, I fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground, then picked up my son.
I did according to the word of the man of God and left with my household for the famine.
When the king of Israel asked me about my son's restoration, I related it to him.
My servant carried my sick boy to me, and he sat on my knees until noon and then died.
Jehovah hid my bitter distress from Elisha and did not tell him.
I reminded Elisha that I had said, “Do not mislead me.”
Gehazi went ahead with Elisha's staff, but my boy did not wake up.
Just as Gehazi was relating how Elisha restored the dead one to life, I arrived appealing for my house and field.
Gehazi told the king of Israel that I was the woman and that this was my son whom Elisha restored to life.
The king of Israel ordered that everything belonging to me be restored, including the produce of my field from the day I left the land.
I was the son of Amaziah and became king of Judah.
The people of Judah made me king when I was 16 years old.
I reigned for 52 years in Jerusalem.
I entered Jehovah's temple to burn incense on the altar of incense.
Leprosy broke out on my forehead while I raged against the priests.
I remained a leper until the day of my death.
My son Jotham judged the people while I stayed in a separate house.
Matthew's genealogy says Joram became father to me, and I became father to Jotham.
My mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
I did what was right just as my father Amaziah had done.
I rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah.
I kept searching for God in the days of Zechariah, who taught me to fear the true God.
While I searched for Jehovah, the true God made me prosper.
I broke through the wall of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod.
I built cities in the territory of Ashdod and among the Philistines.
The Ammonites began to give tribute to me.
My fame spread as far as Egypt.
I built towers in Jerusalem by the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the Buttress.
I built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns.
I loved agriculture.
I had farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in Carmel.
I equipped the army with shields, lances, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and slingstones.
In Jerusalem I made engines of war that could shoot arrows and large stones.
As soon as I was strong, my heart became haughty to my own ruin.
The chief priest and 80 other priests confronted me in the temple.
I had a censer in my hand to burn incense when I became enraged.
They buried me in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, “He is a leper.”
Isaiah's vision came in my days, and in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
Hosea's word came in my days, and in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
The high places were not removed in my days, and the people were still sacrificing and making sacrificial smoke on them.
The true God helped me against the Philistines, the Arabians in Gurbaal, and the Meunim.
I had a great deal of livestock in the Shephelah and on the plain.
The heads of the paternal houses over my mighty warriors numbered 2,600.
Under their command were 307,500 of my men ready for war.
The priests told me it was only for Aaron's descendants to burn incense.
Jehovah afflicted me, and I was excluded from the house of Jehovah.
The rest of my history was recorded by the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz.
I became king in the 27th year of King Jeroboam of Israel.
Amos spoke in my days as king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam of Israel.
Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the officer registered my army under Hananiah.
My engines of war were designed by engineers and set on the towers and corners.
During my rage next to the altar of incense, leprosy broke out before the priests.
I myself hurried out of the temple because Jehovah had struck me.
Jotham did what was right like me, except that he did not invade Jehovah's temple.
In the year I died Isaiah saw Jehovah sitting on a lofty throne.
Zechariah recalls flight from the earthquake that happened in my days.
After Amaziah was laid to rest, I rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah.
I was a widow in Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon.
Elijah asked me for food during the drought.
I had only a handful of flour in the large jar and a little oil in the small jar.
My flour and oil did not run out while Elijah stayed with me.
Elijah restored my dead son to life.
Jehovah commanded me to supply Elijah with food.
Elijah found me gathering pieces of wood at the entrance of the city.
Elijah asked me for a little water in a cup.
As I went to get water, Elijah asked me for a piece of bread.
I said I was about to make something for myself and my son, and then we would die.
Elijah told me first to make him a small round loaf, then something for myself and my son.
Elijah, my household, and I ate for many days.
I swore to Elijah as surely as Jehovah his God was living that I had no bread.
Elijah told me the large jar of flour would not run out and the small jar of oil would not run dry until Jehovah made it rain.
My son's sickness grew so severe that there was no breath left in him.
I asked Elijah whether he had come to bring my error to mind and to put my son to death.
Elijah took my son from my bosom up to the roof chamber.
Elijah brought my son down and said, “See, your son is alive.”
I told Elijah I now knew he was a man of God and that Jehovah's word in his mouth was truth.
Jesus said there were many widows in Israel in Elijah's days, yet Elijah was sent only to me in Zarephath of Sidon.
I fed Elijah after Jehovah had already used ravens to feed him at Cherith.
My son died in my house where the flour and oil had not failed.
